risks: No contact with patients or families. Risks are privacy harm from linking ED, hospital, death and case management data for a stigmatised group, and misuse of findings to cut support; extracts are de-identified at each site and results are reported only in aggregate.
consent: Waiver of individual consent for secondary use of records, approved by the regional ethics board; public notice through each hospital's research transparency page.
data: Site extracts carry study numbers only; linkage keys stay with the regional data custodian; the analysis file is held on the health authority's research server for seven years.
equity: PROGRESS-Plus: frequent attenders include people experiencing homelessness, people with mental illness or addiction, Indigenous people and people without a family doctor. Estimates are reported by family doctor attachment and housing status, community partners review the interpretation, and no subgroup finding is used to exclude people from the program.
effectiveness: The study informs whether case management protects against death and ICU admission; a precise null result is a valid answer for the funding review.
efficiency: Uses existing records and two research assistants; within-site sampling keeps file reading to about 510 hours.
costs: Research assistant time within the approved allocation; data custodian linkage within existing agreements.
grants: None needed; a positive result could support an application to evaluate the program's content.
partnerships: Case managers at the three sites, the regional data custodian, a community organisation serving people experiencing homelessness, and two people with lived knowledge of frequent ED use as advisors.
rebPath: Approved by the regional research ethics board for all three sites on 2026-08-28 (REB-EM-2026-112); data sharing under DSA-2026-044.
limitations: Residual confounding by indication; site differences in files; community sites contribute fewer cases.
summary: Records-only study with a consent waiver, de-identified site extracts and equity reporting.
